summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with a three-day history of epigastric and esophageal burning pain, similar to prior episodes linked to gastrojejunal ulcers and reflux. She remained on tube feeds throughout and was started on IV pantoprazole, cholestyramine, and continued erythromycin for gastric motility. An EGD revealed clean-based ulcers at the gastro-gastric anastomosis, gastric friability, and antral erythema consistent with gastritis. Her symptoms improved with increased acid suppression using pantoprazole twice daily, addition of ranitidine, and continuation of sucralfate. Oral intake was advanced successfully, tube feeds were reduced to baseline, and she was discharged home with medication adjustments and a follow-up appointment. She remained hemodynamically stable throughout, with no complications.
problems: Gastrojejunal ulcer, unspecified as acute or chronic, without hemorrhage or perforation
